survey: A handheld calculator, tilted about 20° and seen almost straight on, floating against a flat yellow background with a π pattern. Main parts: (1) A rounded dark-blue body of even thickness, with a soft drop shadow behind it. (2) A red solar strip of four cells, set flush into the top face near the top edge, right of centre. (3) A grey LCD display in a raised light-grey bezel, set into the upper third of the face and parallel to the body edges. (4) A keypad of 4 rows × 4 keys. Each row has three dark-blue number keys and one cyan function key in the right column. All keys are rounded squares rising from the face, evenly spaced and lined up with the body's tilt. No key overlaps another key or the display. The keys have no symbols, which is an accepted simplification for the card. Nothing hangs loose, there are no cables, and no parts pass through each other. The object floats against an abstract background, which is normal framing for a card, not an unsupported object in a scene.
